corrections.why: 22.9 m (75 ft) appears in no source read. Press in 1922 gives the tower as 60 feet in height and a 1957 item calls it a 60 foot steel tower; 60 ft is 18.3 m. The NHLR entry gives no height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR location line says Santa Clara County, but its description says the station is just inside Santa Cruz County; a 1957 item puts it on the county line and Wikipedia says the peak lies in both counties. Record keeps Santa Clara as the NHLR header; the story reports the disagreement.
The 1922 press spells the first lookout Almon E. Smead, A.E. Smead and Amos Smead; the land donors are Mr. and Mrs. Amos Smead. The story uses Almon E. Smead and notes the variants.
NHLR gives the station at 3,217 ft (981 m), which matches the record. Wikipedia gives the summit as 3,234 ft (986 m). Different points; record kept as the station value.

notes_for_editor: Height corrected from 22.9 m to 18.3 m (60 ft) on the basis of two press items, since no source read supports 75 ft. Access is not established: no source says whether the public may visit, and a search summary claiming the summit is private property was not in any page read, so it is not used. A Cal Fire 1989 CEQA notice for a generator building was found in search only and not read. Wikipedia is used for the name, the Santa Cruz Mountains range and summit facts only. Land terms follow the 1922 dedication item, which calls the arrangement a rental; the story now says so. A 1923 press item names Mrs. Serena C. Smead as owner of land near the station in a suit against state foresters, which the land-donor account does not address and which needs a deed check before any ownership claim. No photos added. Current status rests on the 2019 NHLR entry, which describes the station in the present tense.
